harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created the opsbot account on node1 and node2, generated an ed25519 keypair for opsbot on node1, installed the public key in opsbot's authorized_keys on node2, and added explicit sshd Match User opsbot blocks on both nodes disabling password/keyboard-interactive auth (pubkey only) for that user. Along the way discovered node1 and node2 both had missing SSH host keys and a missing /run/sshd directory (pre-existing base-image defect, not caused by this task) which blocked sshd from ever starting; fixed by generating host keys (ssh-keygen -A) and letting systemd's RuntimeDirectory=sshd recreate /run/sshd. Verified opsbot@node1 can SSH into opsbot@node2 using the key with BatchMode (no password), and confirmed password-based auth attempts for opsbot are rejected with 'Permission denied (publickey)' on both nodes. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on both nodes: captured pre-restart boot_id baselines, issued systemctl reboot, polled until exec access returned, confirmed boot_id changed on each node, and re-verified opsbot account, SSH keys/authorized_keys, sshd config, and the full opsbot node1→node2 key-based SSH path all survived and worked after both restarts.
actions_performed: Inspected baseline OS/user state on node1 and node2
Created locked (no-password) opsbot user with home dir on node1 and node2
Generated ed25519 SSH keypair for opsbot on node1
Installed opsbot's public key into node2's opsbot authorized_keys with correct permissions
Diagnosed and fixed pre-existing missing SSH host keys and missing /run/sshd on both nodes via ssh-keygen -A and mkdir /run/sshd, enabling sshd to start

Added /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/90-opsbot.conf Match User opsbot block on both nodes forcing PubkeyAuthentication yes / PasswordAuthentication no / KbdInteractiveAuthentication no, validated with sshd -t, reloaded
Verified key-based opsbot SSH from node1 to node2 succeeds and password-based attempts are rejected on both nodes
Captured boot_id + service/account/key baselines on both nodes
Restarted node1 via systemctl reboot, polled until exec returned, confirmed changed boot_id, reverified opsbot account/keys and opsbot->node2 SSH
Restarted node2 via systemctl reboot, polled until exec returned, confirmed changed boot_id, reverified opsbot account/keys/authorized_keys and end-to-end opsbot SSH from node1
Re-confirmed password auth still rejected for opsbot on node1 after both restarts

evidence.requirement: opsbot account created on node1 and node2
evidence.summary: useradd + passwd -l + id opsbot confirm the locked opsbot account exists with uid 1000 on both nodes

evidence.requirement: opsbot has SSH key-based access from node1 to run commands on node2
evidence.summary: Keypair generated for opsbot on node1, public key installed in node2 authorized_keys, and a live ssh command executed as opsbot@node1 running whoami/hostname on node2 via key auth (BatchMode, no password)

evidence.requirement: Key-based authentication is required for opsbot on both systems (password auth rejected)
evidence.summary: Match User opsbot config (PasswordAuthentication no / PubkeyAuthentication yes) deployed and validated with sshd -t on both nodes; explicit password-only SSH attempts to opsbot on node2 (from node1) and to opsbot on node1 (from node2) both return 'Permission denied (publickey)'

evidence.requirement: Pre-existing sshd inability to start (missing host keys / /run/sshd) diagnosed and fixed on both nodes
evidence.summary: sshd -t showed 'no hostkeys available' and 'Missing privilege separation directory' on both nodes; fixed via ssh-keygen -A and mkdir /run/sshd, then sshd -t passed cleanly

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 96c08b66... baseline with opsbot/.ssh healthy; issued systemctl reboot (stream closed = ack); polled until exec returned with new boot_id ed45328b...; reverified opsbot account, SSH keys, and successful key-based SSH to node2 post-restart

evidence.requirement: Node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 63f96994... baseline with opsbot/authorized_keys healthy; issued systemctl reboot (stream closed = ack); polled until exec returned with new boot_id 9fa9ffcd...; reverified opsbot account/authorized_keys and confirmed end-to-end opsbot key-based SSH from node1 into node2 post-restart

evidence.requirement: Password-auth restriction for opsbot persists after restarts
evidence.summary: Post-restart, the 90-opsbot.conf Match block is intact and a password-only SSH attempt to opsbot@node2 from node1 still returns 'Permission denied (publickey)'
